top_choice_rationale: Biomolecular phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) is a new physical-chemical principle of molecular organisation: membrane-free compartments as a thermodynamic outcome of multivalency and phase behaviour, with liquid P-granule behaviour shown in 2009 and a quantitative valency framework tested by many laboratories. The maturity objection (which endogenous condensates are true phases, thin in-cell data) is real, but the citation is scoped to the established principle, and it is a concept a chemistry prize can credit as chemistry. Targeted protein degradation (P001) is a close second and a defensible outcome; its science is sound but its PROTAC and glue branches have different origins and no PROTAC drug is yet approved.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my lipid and amyloid work is adjacent to condensate biophysics but involves no apparent direct collaboration with the proposed laureates
